text: Withdrawals are capped at a daily limit of 5000 per account, a threshold the plan never mentions.
The daily withdrawal counter never resets, so the 'daily' limit is in practice a lifetime limit per account.
Transfers out of an account do not count toward the daily withdrawal limit, so the limit can be bypassed by transferring.
Every amount is rounded to two decimal places (cents) using Math.round, i.e. half rounds up toward positive infinity, with floating-point error possible.
The positivity check runs before rounding, so a tiny amount like 0.001 is accepted and recorded as a zero-value operation.
Balances and amounts are stored as floating-point numbers rather than integer cents.
Overdrafts are not allowed: a withdrawal or transfer that would make the balance negative is rejected as insufficient-funds.
When a withdrawal both exceeds the balance and the daily limit, insufficient-funds is reported first.
A repeated transaction id is silently acknowledged as success without checking that the amount, accounts or operation type match the original.
Transaction ids are unique across all accounts and all operation types, and are remembered forever in memory.
Rejected operations do not consume their transaction id, so a retry with the same id after a rejection can later succeed.
Amount validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry of an id with an invalid amount is rejected rather than acknowledged.
Accounts are created automatically on first use by any operation, with no explicit opening required.
A withdrawal or transfer from an unknown account creates that account even when the operation is then rejected.
Querying the balance or history of an unknown account returns 0 or an empty list instead of an error.
Infinity is accepted as a valid positive amount; only NaN, zero and negatives are rejected.
Transaction ids and account ids are not validated, so empty or missing strings are accepted.
A transfer is recorded as two history entries (transfer-out and transfer-in) sharing the same transaction id.
History entries record only the id, kind and amount, with no timestamp, counterparty account or resulting balance.
Rejected operations are returned with a short reason code string and not logged anywhere.
